The first version of this report, and the first implementation of the
occurrence indices it is built on, were produced by Nevio Dubbini at Miningful
Studio ([www.miningfulstudio.eu](http://www.miningfulstudio.eu)). The index
construction documented in Part B, and every sensitivity analysis in Part E,
were added by Yasaman Ranjbaran for the revised manuscript.

<br>

# Scope and what changed

This file reproduces the Herbarium Density Index (HDI) exactly as reported in
the manuscript, and runs each of the sensitivity analyses the paper cites. It
replaces the original exploratory report. The substantive differences from
that report are listed here so that a reader comparing the two can see what
moved and why.

| Element | Original report | This version |
|---|---|---|
| Spatial unit | 0.01 degree bins on raw longitude and latitude | 10 x 10 km cells on ETRS89-LAEA, EPSG:3035 |
| Spatial inequality | `lctools::spGini` on coordinate pairs | sample Gini of specimen counts across occupied cells |
| Gini range | raw `G`, whose complement has a species-specific floor of `1/n` | `G* = G * n/(n-1)`, so `1 - G*` spans `[0, 1]` for every species |
| Unoccupied units | temporal series padded with zeros for every empty decade | both Gini coefficients computed over occupied units only |
| Temporal window | all years present in the file | 1740 to 2019, 28 complete decadal bins anchored to the window start |
| Modern window | all years present in the file | 2000 to 2019, ending with the herbarium series |
| Undated specimens | dropped by `drop_na()` | kept for intensity and the spatial terms, excluded from the temporal terms only |
| Aggregation | first principal component of the six inputs, rescaled 0 to 100 | equally weighted geometric mean of four dimensions, `100 * (I*S*T*O)^(1/4)` |
| Role of the PCA | the index itself | a description of how the six inputs covary, nothing more |
| Overlap | percentage of modern binned locations also present in the herbarium set | unchanged in definition; computed on the 10 km grid, and `NA` rather than `0` when a species has no modern record |
| Sensitivity | none | resolution, weights, functional form, dimension removal, variance decomposition, record resampling |

Two points of substance behind the table. First, the original index was the
first principal component, and the sign of a principal component is arbitrary,
so whether overlap was rewarded or penalised was not fixed by the method. The
revised index states its weights in advance instead. Second, padding the
decadal series with zeros made the temporal Gini largely a restatement of
temporal coverage, a quantity already entering the index separately: in the
original implementation the temporal Gini and the number of occupied decades
correlate at rho = -0.949, against rho = 0.413 here.

<br>

# Part A. Data, grid and the six inputs

## A.1 Configuration

Every constant that the manuscript states is set here and nowhere else.

```{r config}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(sf)
  library(ggplot2)
})

## ---- paths ---------------------------------------------------------------
## Set HDI_BASE to the directory holding the four input files, or leave it and
## place them next to this file. On the cluster this was
## /data/fdalgrande_data/HDI-YASI.
BASE_DIR  <- Sys.getenv("HDI_BASE", ".")
OUT_DIR   <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "HDI_output")
dir.create(OUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

HERB_FILE <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "herbaria_occurrences_filtered.csv")
MOD_FILE  <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "current_occurrences_enriched.csv")
SPP_FILE  <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "species_index_full_info.csv")       # sep = ";"
ATTR_FILE <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "species_index_full_info_all_info.csv")  # sep = ";"

## ---- resolution ----------------------------------------------------------
EPSG_LAEA   <- 3035          # ETRS89 Lambert Azimuthal Equal Area
GRID_KM     <- 10            # EEA reference grid spacing (INSPIRE)
BIN_YR      <- 10            # decadal bins

## ---- windows -------------------------------------------------------------
HERB_WINDOW <- c(1740, 2019) # 28 complete decadal bins; 1700-1739 hold no
                             # dated Alpine specimen in this dataset
MOD_WINDOW  <- c(2000, 2019) # ends with the herbarium series; 2020 onward is
                             # the pandemic recording surge
MOD_LOAD_MAX <- 2025         # loaded, not analysed; needed by one sensitivity run

## ---- conventions ---------------------------------------------------------
UNC_MAX      <- 10000        # coordinateUncertaintyInMeters cutoff, sensitivity only
APPLY_UNC    <- FALSE        # off in the reported analysis
GINI_N1      <- 0            # one occupied unit is trivially even
GINI_CORRECT <- TRUE         # divide G by its attainable maximum (n-1)/n

## ---- sensitivity effort --------------------------------------------------
B_WEIGHTS <- 10000           # Dirichlet draws per concentration
B_BOOT    <- 10000           # record resamples per species
B_VAR     <- 10000           # species resamples for the variance decomposition
ALPHAS    <- c(1, 5, 10, 20, 50)
CORES     <- max(1L, as.integer(Sys.getenv("SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK", "4")))
set.seed(20260928)

## Species excluded after manual review. They are retained in the output table
## with their computed inputs and the reason, and excluded from all statistics.
EXCLUDE <- data.table(
  species = c("Achillea alpina", "Potentilla thyrsiflora"),
  exclusion_reason = c("native to eastern Asia and North America",
                       "no establishment status, probably of hybrid origin"))

setDTthreads(0L)
cat("grid:", GRID_KM, "km   bins:", BIN_YR, "yr   GINI_CORRECT:", GINI_CORRECT, "\n")
```

## A.2 The Gini coefficient and its small-sample correction

A sample Gini cannot reach 1. The most unequal arrangement possible with `n`
units puts every specimen in one unit, which gives `G = (n-1)/n`. The
complement `1 - G` therefore carries a floor of `1/n` that depends on how many
units a species occupies: a species in two cells could never score below 0.50
however concentrated it was, while one in 500 cells could reach 0.002.
Expressing the coefficient as a fraction of its attainable range puts both
evenness terms on `[0, 1]` for every species, matching how the other inputs are
normalised (Damgaard & Weiner 2000; Deltas 2003).

```{r gini}
gini <- function(x, n1 = GINI_N1, correct = GINI_CORRECT) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  if (n == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  if (n == 1L) return(n1)             # one occupied unit: trivially even
  s <- sum(x)
  if (s <= 0) return(NA_real_)
  x <- sort(x)
  g <- sum((2 * seq_len(n) - n - 1) * x) / (n * s)
  if (correct) g <- min(g * n / (n - 1), 1)
  g
}

## verification of the two boundary cases and of the correction itself
cat("perfectly even, 5 units  : G* =", gini(rep(4, 5)), "\n")
cat("all in one of 5 units    : G* =", gini(c(20, 0, 0, 0, 0)), "\n")
cat("uncorrected equivalent   : G  =", gini(c(20, 0, 0, 0, 0), correct = FALSE),
    " = (n-1)/n =", 4/5, "\n")
cat("single occupied unit     : G* =", gini(20), "\n")
```

## A.3 Projection and grid assignment

The Alps span roughly six degrees of latitude, across which the east to west
extent of a cell defined in degrees varies by 10.3%. A degree-based grid would
make the same species appear to occupy more ground in the south than in the
north, so coordinates are projected to an equal-area system before cells are
assigned. The axis-order guard below is not decoration: `sf_project` returning
coordinates in the wrong order produces maps and metrics that look plausible
and are wrong.

```{r project}
add_cells <- function(dt, grid_km, chunk = 2e6) {
  cell_m <- grid_km * 1000
  n  <- nrow(dt)
  gx <- integer(n); gy <- integer(n)
  for (i in seq(1L, n, by = chunk)) {
    j  <- min(i + chunk - 1L, n)
    xy <- sf::sf_project(
      from = "EPSG:4326", to = paste0("EPSG:", EPSG_LAEA),
      pts  = as.matrix(dt[i:j, .(decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)]))
    gx[i:j] <- as.integer(floor(xy[, 1] / cell_m))
    gy[i:j] <- as.integer(floor(xy[, 2] / cell_m))
  }
  dt[, cell := paste(gx, gy, sep = "_")]
  dt[]
}

chk <- sf::sf_project("EPSG:4326", paste0("EPSG:", EPSG_LAEA), cbind(11, 46))
cat("axis check (11E, 46N) -> X", round(chk[1]), " Y", round(chk[2]), "\n")
stopifnot(abs(chk[1] - 4398558) < 5000, abs(chk[2] - 2543530) < 5000)
```

## A.4 Reading the records

Undated specimens are kept. They carry valid coordinates, so they belong in
the specimen count and in both spatial metrics; they are excluded from the
temporal metrics only, where a missing year makes them unusable.

```{r read}
ACC <- data.table(dataset = character(), step = character(),
                  n_records = integer(), n_species = integer())
log_step <- function(dt, dataset, step) {
  ACC <<- rbind(ACC, data.table(
    dataset = dataset, step = step, n_records = nrow(dt),
    n_species = uniqueN(dt$species[!is.na(dt$species) & dt$species != ""])))
  cat(sprintf("%-10s %-42s %12s rows  %6s spp\n", dataset, step,
              format(nrow(dt), big.mark = ","),
              format(uniqueN(dt$species), big.mark = ",")))
}

## ---- species list --------------------------------------------------------
spp <- fread(SPP_FILE, sep = ";")
SP  <- unique(trimws(spp$species)); SP <- SP[nzchar(SP)]
cat("checklist species:", length(SP), "\n\n")

## ---- herbarium -----------------------------------------------------------
h <- fread(HERB_FILE)
if (length(grep("^field_", names(h)))) h[, (grep("^field_", names(h), value = TRUE)) := NULL]
h[, species := trimws(species)]
for (v in c("decimalLatitude", "decimalLongitude", "year",
            "coordinateUncertaintyInMeters"))
  if (v %in% names(h)) set(h, j = v, value = as.numeric(h[[v]]))

log_step(h, "herbarium", "raw file")
h <- h[!is.na(decimalLatitude) & !is.na(decimalLongitude)]
log_step(h, "herbarium", "has coordinates")
h <- h[species %in% SP]
log_step(h, "herbarium", "in the Alpine checklist")

h[, dated := !is.na(year) & year >= HERB_WINDOW[1] & year <= HERB_WINDOW[2]]
cat(sprintf("  undated or outside %d-%d: %s (%.1f%%), kept for intensity and space\n\n",
            HERB_WINDOW[1], HERB_WINDOW[2],
            format(sum(!h$dated), big.mark = ","), 100 * mean(!h$dated)))

## ---- modern --------------------------------------------------------------
m <- fread(MOD_FILE)
m[, species := trimws(species)]
for (v in c("decimalLatitude", "decimalLongitude", "year",
            "coordinateUncertaintyInMeters"))
  if (v %in% names(m)) set(m, j = v, value = as.numeric(m[[v]]))

log_step(m, "modern", "raw file")
m <- m[!is.na(decimalLatitude) & !is.na(decimalLongitude)]
log_step(m, "modern", "has coordinates")
m <- m[species %in% SP]
log_step(m, "modern", "in the Alpine checklist")
m <- m[!is.na(year) & year >= MOD_WINDOW[1] & year <= MOD_LOAD_MAX]
log_step(m, "modern", sprintf("year %d-%d (loaded)", MOD_WINDOW[1], MOD_LOAD_MAX))
log_step(m[year <= MOD_WINDOW[2]], "modern",
         sprintf("year %d-%d (reported analysis)", MOD_WINDOW[1], MOD_WINDOW[2]))

fwrite(ACC, file.path(OUT_DIR, "record_accounting.csv"))
```

## A.5 Provenance of the digitised record

The index measures the archive as currently mobilised, not the physical
holdings of the world's herbaria. These tables are what that claim rests on.

```{r provenance}
if (all(c("institutionCode", "collectionCode") %in% names(h))) {
  by_cols <- intersect(c("institutionCode", "collectionCode", "datasetKey"), names(h))
  ph <- h[, .(records = .N, species = uniqueN(species)), by = by_cols][order(-records)]
  ph[, pct := round(100 * records / sum(records), 3)]
  fwrite(ph, file.path(OUT_DIR, "provenance_herbarium.csv"))
  cat("institutions:", uniqueN(h$institutionCode),
      "   records with no institution code:",
      h[is.na(institutionCode) | institutionCode == "", .N],
      sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(is.na(h$institutionCode) | h$institutionCode == "")))
  print(head(h[, .(records = .N), by = institutionCode][order(-records)], 10))
}
if ("mediaType" %in% names(h))
  cat("\nsheets carrying an image:", round(100 * mean(h$mediaType != ""), 1), "%\n")
```

## A.6 The six inputs and the index, in one function

The six quantities, in the order the manuscript gives them. Two are counts:
the total number of specimens `s`, dated or not, and the number of distinct
10 km cells holding at least one specimen `c`. Two are evenness terms, each
one minus a corrected Gini: spatial evenness `E_s` over specimen counts across
occupied cells, and temporal evenness `E_t` over specimen counts across
occupied decadal bins. Temporal coverage `K` is the number of occupied decadal
bins divided by the 28 available. Historical to modern overlap `v` is the
percentage of a species' contemporary cells that also hold a specimen.

Two conventions decide the behaviour of the evenness terms and are applied
here rather than downstream. Specimens are summed per cell before the Gini is
taken, so the statistic measures how evenly collecting effort is spread rather
than how many cells were visited. And both Gini coefficients are computed over
occupied units only: a cell a species does not occupy is its absence, not
evidence of uneven collecting, and counting it otherwise would conflate range
size with collecting bias and make the statistic depend on where the study
boundary is drawn.

```{r builder}
build_metrics <- function(hh_in, mm_in, grid_km, bin_yr,
                          herb_window = HERB_WINDOW, gini_n1 = GINI_N1,
                          species_list = SP) {

  hh <- add_cells(copy(hh_in), grid_km)
  mm <- add_cells(copy(mm_in), grid_km)

  span   <- herb_window[2] - herb_window[1] + 1
  n_bins <- span / bin_yr
  if (abs(n_bins - round(n_bins)) > 1e-9)
    stop(sprintf("bin width %d does not divide the %d-year window evenly",
                 bin_yr, span))
  n_bins <- as.integer(round(n_bins))

  ## bins anchored to the window start, not to round calendar years, so that
  ## every width tested divides the 280-year span exactly
  hh[dated == TRUE,
     tbin := herb_window[1] + floor((year - herb_window[1]) / bin_yr) * bin_yr]

  ## intensity and space: all sheets. Sheets summed per cell BEFORE the Gini.
  per_cell <- hh[, .(sheets = .N), by = .(species, cell)]
  sp_spat  <- per_cell[, .(n_cells = .N, spatial_gini = gini(sheets, gini_n1)),
                       by = species]
  sp_int   <- hh[, .(n_sheets = .N), by = species]

  ## time: dated sheets, occupied bins only
  per_bin <- hh[dated == TRUE, .(sheets = .N), by = .(species, tbin)]
  sp_temp <- per_bin[, .(n_bins_occupied = .N, n_sheets_dated = sum(sheets),
                         temporal_gini = gini(sheets, gini_n1)), by = species]

  ## modern side and overlap
  mcells <- unique(mm[, .(species, cell)])
  hcells <- unique(hh[, .(species, cell)])
  sp_mod <- mm[, .(n_modern = .N), by = species]

  ov <- merge(mcells[, .(n_cells_modern = .N), by = species],
              hcells[, .(n_cells_herb   = .N), by = species],
              by = "species", all = TRUE)
  inter <- merge(mcells, hcells, by = c("species", "cell"))[
    , .(n_cells_shared = .N), by = species]
  ov <- merge(ov, inter, by = "species", all.x = TRUE)
  for (v in c("n_cells_shared", "n_cells_modern", "n_cells_herb"))
    ov[is.na(get(v)), (v) := 0L]

  ## The denominator is the number of MODERN cells, because the quantity of
  ## interest is how much of a species' present distribution has a historical
  ## baseline. Overlap is undefined, not zero, with no modern records.
  ov[, overlap_pct := fifelse(n_cells_modern > 0,
                              100 * n_cells_shared / n_cells_modern, NA_real_)]
  ov[, `:=`(cells_retained = n_cells_shared,
            cells_lost     = n_cells_herb   - n_cells_shared,
            cells_gained   = n_cells_modern - n_cells_shared)]

  out <- Reduce(function(a, b) merge(a, b, by = "species", all.x = TRUE),
                list(data.table(species = species_list),
                     sp_int, sp_spat, sp_temp, sp_mod, ov))

  for (v in c("n_sheets", "n_cells", "n_bins_occupied", "n_sheets_dated",
              "n_modern", "n_cells_modern", "n_cells_herb", "n_cells_shared",
              "cells_retained", "cells_lost", "cells_gained"))
    out[is.na(get(v)), (v) := 0L]

  ## evenness is reported in place of the Gini, so that higher is better on
  ## all six inputs
  out[, spatial_evenness  := 1 - spatial_gini]
  out[, temporal_evenness := 1 - temporal_gini]
  out[, `:=`(n_bins_possible = n_bins, bin_yr = bin_yr, grid_km = grid_km)]

  ## ---- normalisation ------------------------------------------------------
  ## Three inputs are strongly right-skewed, so a log(1+x) transform precedes
  ## division by the maximum. The transform pulls in the long tail without
  ## changing the order of species. Overlap is divided by log(1+100) because
  ## 100% is its fixed ceiling, not a value observed in this dataset.
  out[, intensity := log1p(n_sheets) / log1p(max(n_sheets, na.rm = TRUE))]
  out[, breadth   := log1p(n_cells)  / log1p(max(n_cells,  na.rm = TRUE))]
  out[, coverage  := pmin(n_bins_occupied / n_bins, 1)]
  out[, overlap   := log1p(overlap_pct) / log1p(100)]

  ## ---- pairing, then aggregation -----------------------------------------
  ## Space and time are each described by two things: how much of it a species
  ## covers, and how evenly its specimens are spread across it. Neither is
  ## sufficient alone, so each pair is a geometric mean.
  out[, spatial  := sqrt(breadth  * spatial_evenness)]
  out[, temporal := sqrt(coverage * temporal_evenness)]
  out[, HDI      := 100 * (intensity * spatial * temporal * overlap)^(1/4)]

  out[, HDI_rank   := frank(-HDI, na.last = "keep")]
  out[, HDI_pctile := round(100 * (1 - (HDI_rank - 1) / sum(!is.na(HDI))), 2)]

  out[, reliability := fifelse(
    n_sheets == 0,                             "no_herbarium_records",
    fifelse(is.na(overlap_pct),                "no_modern_records",
    fifelse(n_cells < 2 | n_bins_occupied < 2, "degenerate_gini",
    fifelse(n_sheets < 5,                      "very_sparse", "ok"))))]
  out[]
}
```

## A.7 The reported run

```{r baseline}
baseline <- build_metrics(h, m[year <= MOD_WINDOW[2]], GRID_KM, BIN_YR)

## species attributes, with an allowlist so that no stale count can travel in
ATTR_COLS <- c("order", "family", "genus", "iucn_assessment", "wcvp_endemic",
               "wcvp_lifeform_description", "wcvp_climate_description",
               "wcvp_introduced", "wcvp_native", "establishment")
if (file.exists(ATTR_FILE)) {
  attr <- fread(ATTR_FILE, sep = ";")
  keep <- intersect(ATTR_COLS, names(attr))
  attr <- unique(attr[, c("species", keep), with = FALSE])
  attr[, species := trimws(species)]
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(attr$species))
  ## guard: nothing that looks like a metric may arrive from a lookup file
  FORBIDDEN <- c("^n_sheets", "^n_cells", "^n_bins", "^n_modern", "^N_samples",
                 "^spatial", "^temporal", "^intensity$", "^breadth$",
                 "^overlap", "^HDI", "^cells_", "^reliability$")
  bad <- keep[vapply(keep, function(cc)
    any(vapply(FORBIDDEN, function(p) grepl(p, cc), logical(1))), logical(1))]
  if (length(bad)) stop("lookup columns look like metrics: ", paste(bad, collapse = ", "))
  stopifnot(length(intersect(keep, names(baseline))) == 0L)
  n0 <- nrow(baseline); hdi0 <- sum(baseline$HDI, na.rm = TRUE)
  baseline <- merge(baseline, attr, by = "species", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
  stopifnot(nrow(baseline) == n0,
            isTRUE(all.equal(sum(baseline$HDI, na.rm = TRUE), hdi0)))
  cat("attributes joined, metrics unchanged\n")
}

## manual exclusions
baseline <- merge(baseline, EXCLUDE, by = "species", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
baseline[, in_analysis := is.na(exclusion_reason)]
cat("species in the checklist :", nrow(baseline), "\n")
cat("excluded after review    :", baseline[in_analysis == FALSE, .N],
    paste0("(", paste(EXCLUDE$species, collapse = ", "), ")"), "\n")

d <- baseline[in_analysis == TRUE]
cat("species analysed         :", nrow(d), "\n")
cat("scored                   :", sum(!is.na(d$HDI)), "\n")

fwrite(baseline, file.path(OUT_DIR, "metrics_complete.csv"))
```

```{r baseline_checks}
cat("=== accounting of the unscored ===\n")
print(d[is.na(HDI), .N, by = reliability][order(-N)])
cat("\n=== reliability flags, all analysed species ===\n")
print(d[, .N, by = reliability][order(-N)])
cat("\n=== the six inputs and the four dimensions ===\n")

print(d[, .(dimension = c("intensity", "spatial", "temporal", "overlap"),
            median = round(c(median(intensity, na.rm = TRUE),

    round(cor(d$n_sheets, d$HDI, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"), 3), "\n")

    round(cor(d$n_sheets, d$n_cells, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"), 3), "\n")

    d[HDI == 0 & overlap_pct == 0, .N], "\n")

## the ceiling: even a species holding all four maxima at once cannot reach 100
cat("\nattainable maximum if one species held every dimension's maximum:",
    round(100 * (max(d$intensity, na.rm = TRUE) * max(d$spatial, na.rm = TRUE) *
                 max(d$temporal,  na.rm = TRUE) * max(d$overlap, na.rm = TRUE))^(1/4), 1), "\n")

FOCAL <- c("Cystopteris fragilis", "Gentiana bavarica", "Larix decidua",
           "Jacobaea uniflora", "Dracocephalum ruyschiana", "Androsace brevis",
           "Callianthemum anemonoides")
print(d[species %in% FOCAL,
        .(species, n_sheets, n_cells, n_bins_occupied,
          sp_even = round(spatial_evenness, 2), tm_even = round(temporal_evenness, 2),
          overlap = round(overlap_pct, 1), HDI = round(HDI, 2), HDI_rank)][order(HDI_rank)])
```

# Part B. What the index is, stated once

```
I  = log(1 + s) / log(1 + s_max)              specimen intensity
Bd = log(1 + c) / log(1 + c_max)              spatial breadth
K  = occupied decadal bins / 28               temporal coverage
O  = log(1 + v) / log(1 + 100)                historical to modern overlap

S  = sqrt(Bd * E_s)                           spatial documentation
T  = sqrt(K  * E_t)                           temporal documentation

HDI = 100 * (I * S * T * O)^(1/4)
```

The four dimensions are multiplied rather than averaged, so a species scoring
near zero on any one of them scores near zero overall. This is intended. A
taxon with abundant specimens but no historical to modern correspondence
cannot support a temporal comparison, and an index in which specimen count
made up for that would recommend it. Equal weights are a stated assumption
rather than an estimate: no external criterion establishes that one dimension
matters more than another, and the OECD and JRC guidance treats equal
weighting as the appropriate default in that situation. Because the choice is
not forced by the data, its effect on the ranking is measured in Part E.

HDI is a relative measure. The normalising maxima come from this dataset, so a
score places a species within the Alpine flora as currently digitised rather
than on an absolute scale, and scores are not comparable across datasets
without recomputation.

<br>

# Part C. The PCA, as a description only

The ordination summarises how the six inputs covary. It does not produce the
index. It is reported because the covariance structure is itself informative,
and because the previous implementation derived the index from it.

```{r pca}
PCA_VARS <- c("intensity", "breadth", "spatial_evenness",
              "coverage", "temporal_evenness", "overlap")
pd <- d[complete.cases(d[, ..PCA_VARS])]
X  <- scale(as.matrix(pd[, ..PCA_VARS]))
pc <- prcomp(X, scale. = FALSE)

cat("=== variance explained ===\n")
print(round(data.frame(sd = pc$sdev,
                       prop = pc$sdev^2 / sum(pc$sdev^2),
                       cum  = cumsum(pc$sdev^2) / sum(pc$sdev^2)), 4))
cat("\n=== loadings, first three components ===\n")
print(round(pc$rotation[, 1:3], 3))

## correlation structure and variance inflation, the reason the pairs are
## multiplied rather than entered separately
CM <- cor(pd[, ..PCA_VARS], use = "complete.obs")
cat("\n=== pairwise correlations ===\n"); print(round(CM, 3))
cat("\nlargest off-diagonal correlation:",
    round(max(abs(CM[upper.tri(CM)])), 3), "\n")
vif <- diag(solve(CM))
cat("\n=== variance inflation factors ===\n"); print(round(vif, 1))
cat("\nCollinearity inflates the variance of ESTIMATED parameters. This index\n",
    "estimates none: the weights are set in advance and the aggregation is a\n",
    "fixed function. What the collinearity does mean is that the dimensions are\n",
    "not independent sources of information, which is why extent and evenness\n",
    "are paired multiplicatively and why Part E.5 measures each dimension's\n",
    "contribution rather than assuming it.\n")

pca_dt <- data.table(PC1 = pc$x[, 1], PC2 = pc$x[, 2], HDI = pd$HDI)
ggplot(pca_dt, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = HDI)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .3, size = .7) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "viridis") +
  labs(title = "The six inputs, summarised",
       subtitle = "The ordination describes covariation; it is not the index") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

## D.3 Alpine endemics

Three tests are reported because the distribution is left-skewed and contains
many zeros, and no single test handles both well.

```{r results_endemic}
if ("wcvp_endemic" %in% names(sc)) {
  e <- copy(sc[!is.na(wcvp_endemic) & wcvp_endemic != "" &
            tolower(as.character(wcvp_endemic)) != "missing data"])
  e[, endemic := fifelse(tolower(as.character(wcvp_endemic)) %in%
                           c("endemic", "true", "yes", "1"), "endemic", "non-endemic")]
  print(e[, .(species = .N, median_HDI = round(median(HDI), 2),
              zero = sum(HDI == 0),
              pct_zero = round(100 * mean(HDI == 0), 1)), by = endemic])

  ## the comparison can only include species that were scored at all
  da <- copy(d[!is.na(wcvp_endemic) & wcvp_endemic != "" &
            tolower(as.character(wcvp_endemic)) != "missing data"])
  da[, endemic := fifelse(tolower(as.character(wcvp_endemic)) %in%
                            c("endemic", "true", "yes", "1"), "endemic", "non-endemic")]
  cat("\nunscorable, which the comparison cannot include:\n")
  print(da[, .(species = .N, unscorable = sum(is.na(HDI)),
               pct = round(100 * mean(is.na(HDI)), 1)), by = endemic])

  x <- e[endemic == "endemic", HDI]; y <- e[endemic == "non-endemic", HDI]
  tt <- t.test(x, y)                      # Welch
  wt <- wilcox.test(x, y)                 # Mann-Whitney U
  cat(sprintf("\nWelch t: t = %.2f, df = %.1f, p = %s, difference in means %.2f\n",
              tt$statistic, tt$parameter, format.pval(tt$p.value, digits = 3),
              unname(tt$estimate[1] - tt$estimate[2])))
  cat(sprintf("Mann-Whitney U: W = %s, p = %s, rank-biserial r = %.3f\n",
              format(wt$statistic, big.mark = ","),
              format.pval(wt$p.value, digits = 3),
              2 * wt$statistic / (length(x) * length(y)) - 1))
  s <- sqrt(((length(x) - 1) * var(x) + (length(y) - 1) * var(y)) /
              (length(x) + length(y) - 2))
  cat(sprintf("Cohen's d: %.3f\n", (mean(x) - mean(y)) / s))

  ## 20% trimmed-mean difference with a bootstrap interval (Yuen 1974)
  tm <- function(v) mean(v, trim = .2)
  obs <- tm(x) - tm(y)
  bs  <- replicate(10000, tm(sample(x, length(x), TRUE)) -
                          tm(sample(y, length(y), TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("20%% trimmed-mean difference: %.2f, 95%% CI %.2f to %.2f\n",
              obs, quantile(bs, .025), quantile(bs, .975)))

  cat("\nwhere the deficit sits, median of each input:\n")
  print(e[, .(specimens = median(n_sheets), cells = median(n_cells),
              decades = median(n_bins_occupied),
              sp_even = round(median(spatial_evenness, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
              tm_even = round(median(temporal_evenness, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
              overlap = round(median(overlap_pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1)), by = endemic])
}
```

## D.5 Taxonomic order

Reported as a negative result. An order is a nomenclatural rank, not an
ecological unit, and with this many species a significance test will detect
almost any structure, so the effect size is what matters.

```{r results_order}
if ("order" %in% names(sc)) {
  o <- sc[!is.na(order) & order != ""]
  keep <- o[, .N, by = order][N >= 3, order]
  o <- o[order %in% keep]
  cat("orders with at least three species:", length(keep),
      "  species:", nrow(o), "\n")
  k <- kruskal.test(HDI ~ factor(order), data = o)
  cat(sprintf("Kruskal-Wallis: H = %.1f, df = %d, p = %s\n",
              k$statistic, k$parameter, format.pval(k$p.value, digits = 3)))
  ss <- summary(aov(HDI ~ factor(order), data = o))
  r2 <- ss[[1]][1, "Sum Sq"] / sum(ss[[1]][, "Sum Sq"])
  cat(sprintf("variance in HDI attributable to order: %.1f%%, leaving %.1f%% within orders\n",
              100 * r2, 100 * (1 - r2)))

  big <- o[, .(n = .N, median_HDI = round(median(HDI), 2),
               iqr = round(IQR(HDI), 2)), by = order][n >= 10][order(-median_HDI)]
  print(big)

  ## is a small order's high median an artefact of its size?
  per <- o[, .(n = .N, med = median(HDI), spread = IQR(HDI)), by = order]
  cat(sprintf("\nmedian HDI against order size:   rho = %.3f, p = %s\n",
              cor(per$n, per$med, method = "spearman"),
              format.pval(cor.test(per$n, per$med, method = "spearman")$p.value, digits = 3)))
  cat(sprintf("spread of HDI against order size: rho = %.3f, p = %s\n",
              cor(per$n, per$spread, method = "spearman"),
              format.pval(cor.test(per$n, per$spread, method = "spearman")$p.value, digits = 3)))
  cat("A positive second correlation with a null first one means small orders\n",
      "look high and homogeneous because they are too small to express the\n",
      "heterogeneity larger orders reveal.\n")
}
```

# Part E. Sensitivity analyses

Four construction choices could have been made differently: the resolution at
which the inputs are computed, the weight given to each dimension, the
functional form of the aggregation, and whether each dimension earns its
place. Each is tested below, followed by two analyses that ask which dimension
drives the ranking and how precisely a single species can be placed.

## E.1 Resolution: grid size and bin width

Grid size enters only the spatial metrics and bin width only the temporal
ones, so the two cannot interact at the input level and a full factorial would
add nothing the marginals do not already give. One extreme corner is included
anyway, because HDI is a product and small shifts in separate terms can
compound in the aggregate score.

Bin widths of 5, 10, 20 and 40 years are tested and 50 is not: 280 / 50 = 5.6
would leave a partial final bin and make the coverage term incomparable across
settings.

```{r sens_settings}
RUNS <- rbindlist(list(
  data.table(dir = "baseline_grid10km_bin10yr", grid_km = GRID_KM, bin_yr = BIN_YR, unc = FALSE, mod_end = 2019),
  data.table(dir = "grid01km",                  grid_km = 1,       bin_yr = BIN_YR, unc = FALSE, mod_end = 2019),
  data.table(dir = "grid05km",                  grid_km = 5,       bin_yr = BIN_YR, unc = FALSE, mod_end = 2019),
  data.table(dir = "grid25km",                  grid_km = 25,      bin_yr = BIN_YR, unc = FALSE, mod_end = 2019),
  data.table(dir = "bin05yr",                   grid_km = GRID_KM, bin_yr = 5,      unc = FALSE, mod_end = 2019),
  data.table(dir = "bin20yr",                   grid_km = GRID_KM, bin_yr = 20,     unc = FALSE, mod_end = 2019),
  data.table(dir = "bin40yr",                   grid_km = GRID_KM, bin_yr = 40,     unc = FALSE, mod_end = 2019),
  data.table(dir = "uncertainty_filter",        grid_km = GRID_KM, bin_yr = BIN_YR, unc = TRUE,  mod_end = 2019),
  data.table(dir = "window_to2025",             grid_km = GRID_KM, bin_yr = BIN_YR, unc = FALSE, mod_end = 2025),
  data.table(dir = "corner_grid01km_bin40yr",   grid_km = 1,       bin_yr = 40,     unc = FALSE, mod_end = 2019)))

keep_sp <- d$species            # the analysed set, so exclusions stay excluded
settings <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(RUNS))) {
  s  <- RUNS[i]
  hs <- h; ms <- m
  if (s$unc) {
    if (!all(c("coordinateUncertaintyInMeters") %in% names(h)) ||
        !all(c("coordinateUncertaintyInMeters") %in% names(m)))
      stop("the uncertainty run needs coordinateUncertaintyInMeters in both files")
    hs <- h[is.na(coordinateUncertaintyInMeters) | coordinateUncertaintyInMeters <= UNC_MAX]
    ms <- m[is.na(coordinateUncertaintyInMeters) | coordinateUncertaintyInMeters <= UNC_MAX]
  }
  ms <- ms[year <= s$mod_end]
  r  <- build_metrics(hs, ms, s$grid_km, s$bin_yr)[species %in% keep_sp]
  settings[[s$dir]] <- r[!is.na(HDI), .(species, HDI)]
  fwrite(r, file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("metrics_", s$dir, ".csv")))
  cat(sprintf("[%2d/%2d] %-28s grid %2d km  bins %2d yr  unc %-5s modern<=%d  scored %d\n",
              i, nrow(RUNS), s$dir, s$grid_km, s$bin_yr, s$unc, s$mod_end, nrow(settings[[s$dir]])))
}

bse <- copy(settings[["baseline_grid10km_bin10yr"]]); setnames(bse, "HDI", "HDI_base")
set_res <- rbindlist(lapply(names(settings), function(nm) {
  j <- merge(bse, settings[[nm]], by = "species")
  j[, `:=`(rb = frank(-HDI_base, ties.method = "average"),
           rr = frank(-HDI,      ties.method = "average"))]
  j[, sh := abs(rb - rr)]
  data.table(run = nm, n_scored = nrow(settings[[nm]]), n_shared = nrow(j),
             median_HDI = round(median(settings[[nm]]$HDI), 2),
             rho = round(cor(j$HDI_base, j$HDI, method = "spearman"), 4),
             median_shift = median(j$sh),
             q90_shift = as.numeric(quantile(j$sh, .9)),
             top20_kept = length(intersect(j[order(rb)][1:20, species],
                                           j[order(rr)][1:20, species])))
}))
setorder(set_res, -rho)
print(set_res)
fwrite(set_res, file.path(OUT_DIR, "sensitivity_settings.csv"))

nb <- set_res[run != "baseline_grid10km_bin10yr"]
cat(sprintf("\nrho against the reported ranking: %.3f to %.3f across %d alternatives\n",
            min(nb$rho), max(nb$rho), nrow(nb)))
cat(sprintf("at least 0.975 in %d of %d; worst: %s (rho %.3f)\n",
            nb[rho >= .975, .N], nrow(nb), nb[which.min(rho), run], min(nb$rho)))
cat("\nAt a 1 km grid almost every specimen occupies a cell of its own, so the\n",
    "occupied-cell count restates the specimen count and the spatial evenness\n",
    "term degenerates, a cell holding a single record being read as perfectly\n",
    "even. The degradation is informative rather than troubling: it reproduces\n",
    "the behaviour of the earlier 0.01 degree implementation and shows directly\n",
    "why a coarser reference grid is appropriate.\n")
```

## E.2 Weights

Equal weighting is a stated assumption, so the question is what any other
defensible weighting would do. Weight vectors are drawn from a Dirichlet
distribution centred on equal weights at five concentrations. The 2.5th
percentile of the resulting rank correlations is reported rather than the
minimum, which keeps falling as more draws are taken.

```{r sens_weights}
DIMS <- c("intensity", "spatial", "temporal", "overlap")
pos  <- d[complete.cases(d[, ..DIMS])]
pos  <- pos[Reduce(`&`, lapply(DIMS, function(cc) pos[[cc]] > 0))]
cat("species with every dimension above zero:", nrow(pos), "\n")

LX  <- log(as.matrix(pos[, ..DIMS]))
H0  <- 100 * exp(rowMeans(LX))
rk0 <- frank(-H0, ties.method = "average")

ddir <- function(n, k, a) { G <- matrix(rgamma(n * k, shape = a, rate = 1), nrow = n); G / rowSums(G) }

wt_res <- rbindlist(lapply(ALPHAS, function(a) {
  W  <- ddir(B_WEIGHTS, length(DIMS), a)
  S  <- LX %*% t(W)
  rh <- as.vector(cor(H0, S, method = "spearman"))
  pick <- sample.int(B_WEIGHTS, min(300L, B_WEIGHTS))
  RK <- apply(S[, pick, drop = FALSE], 2, function(v) frank(-v, ties.method = "average"))
  data.table(alpha = a,
             weight_lo95 = round(quantile(W, .025), 3),
             weight_hi95 = round(quantile(W, .975), 3),
             rho_q025    = round(quantile(rh, .025), 3),
             rho_median  = round(median(rh), 3),
             pct_above_0.95 = round(100 * mean(rh >= .95), 1),
             median_shift = round(median(apply(abs(RK - rk0), 2, median))),
             median_rank_width = round(median(apply(RK, 1, function(r)
               diff(quantile(r, c(.025, .975)))))))
}))
print(wt_res)
fwrite(wt_res, file.path(OUT_DIR, "sensitivity_weights.csv"))
cat("\nThe reported index is unchanged by this analysis. Averaging over\n",
    "arbitrary weightings would replace a stated choice with an unstated one.\n")
```

## E.3 Functional form

Four ways of combining the same four dimensions. The inputs are held fixed and
only the arithmetic changes, so any difference is caused by the form alone.

```{r sens_form}
FD <- copy(d[complete.cases(d[, ..DIMS])])
XF <- as.matrix(FD[, ..DIMS])
FD[, f_mult := 100 * apply(XF, 1, function(r) prod(r)^(1/4))]        # adopted
FD[, f_add  := 100 * rowMeans(XF)]                                   # compensatory
FD[, f_noov := 100 * apply(XF[, 1:3, drop = FALSE], 1, function(r) prod(r)^(1/3))]
pcf <- prcomp(XF, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
s1  <- pcf$x[, 1]; if (cor(s1, FD$f_mult) < 0) s1 <- -s1
FD[, f_pc1 := 100 * (s1 - min(s1)) / (max(s1) - min(s1))]

FORMS <- c(multiplicative = "f_mult", arithmetic = "f_add",
           no_overlap = "f_noov", first_PC = "f_pc1")
form_res <- rbindlist(lapply(names(FORMS), function(k) {
  v <- FD[[FORMS[k]]]
  data.table(form = k,
             median = round(median(v), 2),
             rho_vs_adopted = round(cor(v, FD$f_mult, method = "spearman"), 3),
             median_rank_shift = median(abs(frank(-v, ties.method = "average") -
                                            frank(-FD$f_mult, ties.method = "average"))),
             rho_vs_specimen_count = round(cor(v, FD$n_sheets, method = "spearman"), 3))
}))
print(form_res)
fwrite(form_res, file.path(OUT_DIR, "sensitivity_formulations.csv"))

cat("\nspecies the arithmetic mean rescues, that is, where one dimension buys\n",
    "off another:\n")
FD[, gained := frank(-f_mult, ties.method = "average") -
               frank(-f_add,  ties.method = "average")]
print(FD[order(-gained)][1:10, .(species, n_sheets, overlap = round(overlap_pct, 1),
         intensity = round(intensity, 2), overlap_term = round(overlap, 2),
         gained)])
cat("\nThe forms agree closely over the whole ranking, so the geometric mean is\n",
    "defended on its rationale rather than on its aggregate effect: a species\n",
    "must be adequate on all four dimensions. It continues to decide where the\n",
    "extreme species land, which is where it is meant to act.\n")
```

## E.4 Removing a dimension

The hardest version of the question: remove a dimension and also allow any
reasonable weighting of what is left.

```{r sens_dropone}
LEVELS <- list(
  dimensions = list(cols = DIMS, coef = rep(1/4, 4)),
  inputs     = list(cols = c("intensity", "breadth", "spatial_evenness",
                             "coverage", "temporal_evenness", "overlap"),
                    coef = c(1/4, 1/8, 1/8, 1/8, 1/8, 1/4)))

run_loo <- function(lv, label) {
  cols <- lv$cols; coef <- lv$coef; k <- length(cols)
  stopifnot(abs(sum(coef) - 1) < 1e-12)
  x  <- d[complete.cases(d[, ..cols])]
  x  <- x[Reduce(`&`, lapply(cols, function(cc) x[[cc]] > 0))]
  M  <- log(as.matrix(x[, ..cols]))
  Lf <- as.vector(M %*% coef)
  rkf <- frank(-Lf, ties.method = "average")
  cat("\n---", label, ":", nrow(M), "species with every component above zero ---\n")

  res <- rbindlist(lapply(c(1, 10, 50), function(a) rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(k), function(j) {
    W  <- ddir(B_WEIGHTS, k - 1L, a)
    S  <- M[, -j, drop = FALSE] %*% t(W)
    rh <- as.vector(cor(Lf, S, method = "spearman"))   # Spearman is invariant to exp()
    pick <- sample.int(B_WEIGHTS, min(200L, B_WEIGHTS))
    sh <- vapply(pick, function(b)
      median(abs(frank(-S[, b], ties.method = "average") - rkf)), numeric(1))
    t20 <- vapply(pick[1:min(50, length(pick))], function(b)
      length(intersect(x$species[order(rkf)][1:20],
                       x$species[order(frank(-S[, b], ties.method = "average"))][1:20])),
      numeric(1))
    data.table(alpha = a, dropped = cols[j],
               rho_q025 = round(quantile(rh, .025), 4),
               rho_med  = round(median(rh), 4),
               median_rank_shift = round(median(sh)),
               top20_kept_med = round(median(t20)))
  }))))
  setorder(res, alpha, rho_med)
  print(res)
  fwrite(res, file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("sensitivity_dropone_", label, ".csv")))
  res
}
loo_dim <- run_loo(LEVELS$dimensions, "dimensions")
loo_inp <- run_loo(LEVELS$inputs,     "inputs")

s10 <- loo_dim[alpha == 10][order(rho_med)]
cat(sprintf("\nat alpha = 10, removing %s changes the ranking most (median rho %.3f,\nmedian shift %d positions); removing %s changes it least (rho %.3f)\n",
            s10$dropped[1], s10$rho_med[1], s10$median_rank_shift[1],
            s10$dropped[.N], s10$rho_med[.N]))
cat("A dimension that correlates strongly with the others can be removed with\n",
    "little effect simply because they stand in for it. Read this alongside\n",
    "E.5, which is not affected by that.\n")
```

## E.5 Which dimension drives the spread, with intervals

The spread in scores is divided into shares that sum to 100%, one per
dimension, by decomposing the variance of log HDI by factor component
(Shorrocks 1982). Because the shares are covariances with the total, a
component acting as a correction to another can take a negative share. The
decomposition is bootstrapped over resamples of the species so that each share
carries an interval.

```{r sens_variance}
run_var <- function(lv, label) {
  cols <- lv$cols; coef <- lv$coef; k <- length(cols)
  x  <- d[complete.cases(d[, ..cols])]
  x  <- x[Reduce(`&`, lapply(cols, function(cc) x[[cc]] > 0))]
  M  <- log(as.matrix(x[, ..cols])); n <- nrow(M)
  cat("\n---", label, ":", n, "species ---\n")

  one <- function(idx) {
    Mi <- M[idx, , drop = FALSE]
    li <- as.vector(Mi %*% coef)
    V  <- var(li)
    vapply(seq_len(k), function(j) cov(Mi[, j] * coef[j], li) / V, numeric(1))
  }
  obs <- one(seq_len(n))
  SH  <- vapply(seq_len(B_VAR), function(b) one(sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)),
                numeric(k))
  q   <- t(apply(SH, 1, quantile, c(.025, .975), na.rm = TRUE))
  tab <- data.table(component = cols, elasticity = round(coef, 3),
                    share_pct = round(100 * obs, 1),
                    ci_lo = round(100 * q[, 1], 1),
                    ci_hi = round(100 * q[, 2], 1),
                    largest_in_pct_of_resamples =
                      round(100 * tabulate(apply(SH, 2, which.max), nbins = k) / B_VAR, 1))
  setorder(tab, -share_pct)
  print(tab)
  fwrite(tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("sensitivity_variance_", label, ".csv")))
  ord <- order(-obs)
  cat(sprintf("leader against runner-up: %s had the larger share in %.1f%% of resamples\n",
              cols[ord[1]], 100 * mean(SH[ord[1], ] > SH[ord[2], ], na.rm = TRUE)))
  tab
}
var_dim <- run_var(LEVELS$dimensions, "dimensions")
var_inp <- run_var(LEVELS$inputs,     "inputs")

cat("\nThe two analyses answer different questions and both are reported.\n",
    "Specimen intensity generates most of the spread in scores, because counts\n",
    "differ by orders of magnitude across the flora. Overlap generates most of\n",
    "the distinctions, because nothing else in the index records whether the\n",
    "historical and the modern records fall in the same places. A species with\n",
    "many specimens usually occupies many cells, so when intensity is removed\n",
    "spatial breadth substitutes for much of it; when overlap goes, nothing\n",
    "replaces it. Equal weights therefore do not give equal influence.\n")
```

## E.6 How precisely can one species be placed

Each species' own records are resampled with replacement and the index
recomputed. Every replicate holds the same number of specimens as the
original, drawn at random with replacement, so about a third of the originals
are absent from any one replicate while others appear twice. The specimen
count is unchanged; what varies is how the specimens fall across cells and
decades. Records are drawn as a multinomial over the cell and bin pairs the
species occupies, which is equivalent to resampling the records themselves and
far faster.

This treats the sheets that exist as the population. It measures how much a
score leans on individual specimens, not what would have happened had
collectors visited different valleys. The second question cannot be answered
from these data, and saying so is stronger than implying the interval covers
it.

```{r sens_bootstrap}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(parallel))

## vectorised Gini over a matrix of count columns, same correction as gini()
gini_mat <- function(M, n1 = GINI_N1, correct = GINI_CORRECT) {
  k <- nrow(M); S <- colSums(M); mm <- colSums(M > 0)
  if (k == 1L) return(ifelse(S > 0, n1, NA_real_))
  Ms <- apply(M, 2L, sort)
  if (is.null(dim(Ms))) Ms <- matrix(Ms, nrow = k)
  A <- colSums(Ms * seq_len(k))
  G <- (2 * A - (2 * k - mm + 1) * S) / (mm * S)
  G[mm <= 1L] <- n1
  G[S <= 0]   <- NA_real_
  if (correct) { ok <- which(mm > 1L); G[ok] <- pmin(G[ok] * mm[ok] / (mm[ok] - 1), 1) }
  G
}
## agreement with the scalar version, on a case with ties and a zero
stopifnot(abs(gini_mat(matrix(c(5, 3, 0, 1), ncol = 1)) - gini(c(5, 3, 0, 1))) < 1e-12)

hb <- add_cells(copy(h), GRID_KM)
hb[, tbin := fifelse(dated, HERB_WINDOW[1] +
                       floor((year - HERB_WINDOW[1]) / BIN_YR) * BIN_YR, NA_integer_)]
mb <- add_cells(copy(m[year <= MOD_WINDOW[2]]), GRID_KM)
modc <- unique(mb[, .(species, cell)])
nmod <- modc[, .(n_cells_modern = .N), by = species]

## only species that received a score can carry an interval
boot_sp <- d[!is.na(HDI), species]
cmb <- hb[species %in% boot_sp, .(n = .N), by = .(species, cell, tbin)]
cmb <- merge(cmb, modc[, .(species, cell, in_mod = TRUE)],
             by = c("species", "cell"), all.x = TRUE)
cmb[is.na(in_mod), in_mod := FALSE]
cmb <- merge(cmb, nmod, by = "species", all.x = TRUE)

MAXS   <- max(d$n_sheets, na.rm = TRUE)
MAXC   <- max(d$n_cells,  na.rm = TRUE)
N_BINS <- d$n_bins_possible[1]
cat("normalisation maxima held fixed at the reported values: sheets", MAXS,
    " cells", MAXC, " bins", N_BINS, "\n")

boot_one <- function(dt) {
  N <- sum(dt$n); ncm <- dt$n_cells_modern[1]
  M <- rmultinom(B_BOOT, N, prob = dt$n / N)
  ci <- as.integer(factor(dt$cell))
  CM <- rowsum(M, ci)
  n_cells <- colSums(CM > 0)
  gS <- gini_mat(CM)
  cell_mod <- tapply(dt$in_mod, ci, any)
  shared <- colSums(CM[as.logical(cell_mod), , drop = FALSE] > 0)
  ov_pct <- if (is.na(ncm) || ncm <= 0) rep(NA_real_, B_BOOT) else 100 * shared / ncm
  dd <- !is.na(dt$tbin)
  if (any(dd)) {
    bi <- as.integer(factor(dt$tbin[dd]))
    BM <- rowsum(M[dd, , drop = FALSE], bi)
    n_bins <- colSums(BM > 0); gT <- gini_mat(BM)
  } else { n_bins <- rep(0L, B_BOOT); gT <- rep(NA_real_, B_BOOT) }
  I  <- log1p(N) / log1p(MAXS)
  Bd <- log1p(n_cells) / log1p(MAXC)
  S  <- sqrt(Bd * (1 - gS))
  Tt <- sqrt(pmin(n_bins / N_BINS, 1) * (1 - gT))
  O  <- log1p(ov_pct) / log1p(100)
  100 * (I * S * Tt * O)^(1/4)
}

sp  <- split(cmb, cmb$species)
res <- mclapply(sp, boot_one, mc.cores = CORES)

Hm <- do.call(rbind, res)
bt <- data.table(species = names(res),
                 HDI_lo95 = apply(Hm, 1, quantile, .025, na.rm = TRUE),
                 HDI_med  = apply(Hm, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE),
                 HDI_hi95 = apply(Hm, 1, quantile, .975, na.rm = TRUE))
RK <- apply(-Hm, 2, frank, ties.method = "average", na.last = "keep")
bt[, `:=`(rank_lo95 = apply(RK, 1, quantile, .025, na.rm = TRUE),
          rank_hi95 = apply(RK, 1, quantile, .975, na.rm = TRUE))]
bt[, `:=`(HDI_width = HDI_hi95 - HDI_lo95, rank_width = rank_hi95 - rank_lo95)]
bt <- merge(bt, d[, .(species, HDI, HDI_rank, n_sheets, n_cells, n_bins_occupied)],
            by = "species", all.x = TRUE)
setorder(bt, HDI_rank)
fwrite(bt, file.path(OUT_DIR, "sensitivity_bootstrap.csv"))

cat(sprintf("\nmedian 95%% rank interval: %d positions of %d\n",
            round(median(bt$rank_width, na.rm = TRUE)), sum(!is.na(d$HDI))))
cat(sprintf("median 95%% HDI interval : %.2f points\n",
            median(bt$HDI_width, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("within the top 20, median rank interval: %d positions\n",
            round(median(bt[HDI_rank <= 20, rank_width], na.rm = TRUE))))
cat("\ninterval width by specimen count:\n")
print(bt[, .(species = .N,
             median_rank_width = round(median(rank_width, na.rm = TRUE)),
             median_HDI_width  = round(median(HDI_width, na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
         by = .(sheets = cut(n_sheets, c(0, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 1000, Inf),
                labels = c("1-10", "11-25", "26-50", "51-100", "101-250",
                           "251-1000", "1000+")))][order(sheets)])
cat("\nWidth is greatest in the middle of the specimen range. The sparsest\n",
    "species are held near the bottom by their other inputs and cannot move\n",
    "far, which is why their intervals are narrow rather than reassuring.\n")
```

## E.7 One table covering every axis

```{r sens_master}
master <- rbindlist(list(
  data.table(axis = "1. Grid and bin resolution",
             what = sprintf("%d alternative settings", nrow(nb)),
             rho_worst = min(nb$rho), rho_median = median(nb$rho),
             detail = sprintf("worst: %s", nb[which.min(rho), run])),
  data.table(axis = "2. Dimension weights",
             what = sprintf("Dirichlet sweep, alpha %s",
                            paste(range(ALPHAS), collapse = " to ")),
             rho_worst = wt_res[alpha == min(ALPHAS), rho_q025],
             rho_median = wt_res[alpha == 10, rho_median],
             detail = sprintf("at alpha = 10, weights %.2f to %.2f",
                              wt_res[alpha == 10, weight_lo95],
                              wt_res[alpha == 10, weight_hi95])),
  data.table(axis = "3. Functional form",
             what = sprintf("%d alternative forms", nrow(form_res) - 1L),
             rho_worst = min(form_res[form != "multiplicative", rho_vs_adopted]),
             rho_median = median(form_res[form != "multiplicative", rho_vs_adopted]),
             detail = sprintf("arithmetic mean %.3f",
                              form_res[form == "arithmetic", rho_vs_adopted])),
  data.table(axis = "4. Removing a dimension",
             what = "each of 4 removed, the rest reweighted",
             rho_worst = min(loo_dim[alpha == 10, rho_med]),
             rho_median = median(loo_dim[alpha == 10, rho_med]),
             detail = sprintf("most influential: %s",
                              loo_dim[alpha == 10][which.min(rho_med), dropped]))))
master[, `:=`(rho_worst = round(rho_worst, 3), rho_median = round(rho_median, 3))]
print(master)
fwrite(master, file.path(OUT_DIR, "sensitivity_master.csv"))

cat("\nThe bootstrap is reported separately. It produces intervals rather than a\n",
    "correlation and answers a different question: not whether the ranking as a\n",
    "whole survives a different construction, but how firmly one species sits\n",
    "where it does.\n")
```

# Companion scripts

The figures and the remaining descriptive analyses in the manuscript are
produced by the following scripts, which read `metrics_complete.csv` written
above and recompute nothing.

| Script | Produces |
|---|---|
| `16_results.R` | HDI distribution, the four dimensions, endemics, taxonomic order |
| `20_ridges.R` | collection-history ridges at three positions on the index |
| `21_maps.R` | collecting effort, effort by era, and per-species occupancy on the same 10 km grid |
| `22_use_cases.R` | overlap against temporal coverage, the two study designs |
| `23_retention.R` | what each HDI threshold retains, by group |
| `24_elevation.R` | documentation against altitude; writes `species_elevation.csv` |
| `26_threeD.R` | the three-dimensional views |
| `27_collecting_curve.R` | two and a half centuries of collecting effort |
| `28_elevation_panels.R` | specimen elevation and species richness per band |
